comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's live 2026-2027 study guide, checked 2026-10-03, identifies BSc Technische Wiskunde (B-TW, CROHO 56965) as a three-year, 180-EC programme. For cohorts starting in 2024-25 or later it defines twelve 5-EC first-year courses; twelve 5-EC second-year courses, including two electives; and a third year comprising a 30-EC minor, three 5-EC electives and a 15-EC bachelor project. The live programme overview supplies the named compulsory first- and second-year courses and the restricted elective pool. Bewijstechnieken is published as linked 3-EC theory and 2-EC practical parts and is retained as one 5-EC curricular unit below. Genuine elective and minor space remains generic rather than inventing choices.

exception.reason: TU Delft Applied Mathematics is a cumulative proof-based mathematics degree. Its compulsory spine includes two analysis courses followed by real and complex analysis, two linear-algebra courses, algebra, discrete mathematics, ordinary and partial differential equations, numerical methods, optimisation, probability, statistics and measure-theoretic probability, alongside four modelling courses, programming and proof techniques. Restricted upper-level mathematics electives and a 15-EC mathematics bachelor project complete that formation. UCR offers a useful applied mathematics, statistics, programming and data-science sequence, but it does not provide the proof-intensive real/complex analysis, measure theory, abstract algebra and PDE depth or the mathematics-specific capstone environment required to preserve this degree's academic identity. A 24-course UCR response would become an interdisciplinary quantitative and data-science pathway rather than Applied Mathematics.
exception.curriculumContext: The current cohort structure accounts for all 180 EC: year one is twelve 5-EC curricular units (with Proof Techniques delivered as 3-EC theory plus 2-EC practical); year two is ten named compulsory 5-EC courses plus two 5-EC restricted electives; and year three is a 30-EC minor, three 5-EC restricted electives and a 15-EC Bachelor Project. The study guide identifies the programme's mathematical domains as analysis, stochastics, optimisation and discrete mathematics, numerical methods and differential equations, plus modelling and applications. No named graduation route requires selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide meaningful applied quantitative foundations. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal logic and discrete structures, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISDATA111/211/311 add programming, data science, machine learning and advanced data analysis. The workbook nevertheless has no sustained proof-based sequence in real and complex analysis, measure theory, abstract algebra or topology; no dedicated partial-differential-equations course; and no mathematics-specific independent research project comparable to the 15-EC bachelor project. The available courses support a coherent interdisciplinary applied-mathematics and data-science pathway, but cannot supply the target's dense compulsory pure-and-applied mathematics progression without replacing its defining upper mathematics with adjacent computing and data-science study.
